source.analysis_subject: bench: reject Decode M1 table-free E2M1

scan.nonfinite_interpretation: raw one-byte E4M3FN codes; this scan classifies lossless code payloads and does not decode values

direct_base_plus_delta.rule: bits is the smallest of 5, 6, 7, or 8 for which max_code - min_code is at most 2^bits - 1

dictionary_index.rule: bits is the smallest of 5, 6, 7, or 8 that can index every distinct raw code in the layer

direct_adaptive_ceiling.assumption: ideal padding-free payload with the existing 53 six-bit layers and direct seven-bit base-plus-delta payloads for the 11 current fallbacks
direct_adaptive_ceiling.excluded_costs: seven-bit unpack, packing, alignment, descriptor, and dispatch overhead are all treated as zero

dictionary_ceiling.assumption: ideal dense per-layer dictionary indices: 63 layers at six bits and one layer at seven bits, before any codebook, padding, metadata, or lookup cost
dictionary_ceiling.excluded_costs: per-layer codebooks, index remapping, lookup/unpack instructions, padding, metadata, packing, and dispatch overhead are all treated as zero

decision.reason: Even padding-free direct adaptive widths save only 2.709359606% of the current hot scale payload and optimistically project to a 0.027813500-ms/token median. The more aggressive dictionary-index ideal saves only 5.172413793% before codebooks and optimistically projects to 0.053098500 ms/token. Both miss the 15% byte and 0.30-ms/token admission gates before paying new unpack or lookup overhead.
decision.reopen_when: Only a materially different lossless representation or fused consumer with a new exact scan showing at least 15% hot-payload reduction and a credible at-least-0.30-ms/token Decode contribution.

reproduction.shell: bash invoking Perl core JSON::PP; no model or repository file is modified
reproduction.command:
Q3X_SCALE_SCAN_MODEL_DIR=/home/rm01/models/dev/llm/nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 perl -MJSON::PP=decode_json -e 'use strict; use warnings; my $dir=$ENV{Q3X_SCALE_SCAN_MODEL_DIR}; my(@rows,%unique,%bits); for my $path(sort glob("$dir/model-*.safetensors")){open my $fh,"<:raw",$path or die $!; read($fh,my $prefix,8)==8 or die "short prefix"; my $header_len=unpack("Q<",$prefix); read($fh,my $header,$header_len)==$header_len or die "short header"; my $meta=decode_json($header); for my $name(keys %$meta){next unless $name=~/^model\.language_model\.layers\.(\d+)\.mlp\.down_proj\.weight_scale$/; my $layer=0+$1; my($start,$end)=@{$meta->{$name}{data_offsets}}; my $bytes=$end-$start; die "unexpected tensor" unless $meta->{$name}{dtype} eq "F8_E4M3" && join("x",@{$meta->{$name}{shape}}) eq "5120x1088" && $bytes==5570560; seek($fh,8+$header_len+$start,0) or die "seek"; my($min,$max)=(255,0); my %seen; my $left=$bytes; while($left){my $want=$left>1048576?1048576:$left; read($fh,my $buf,$want)==$want or die "short payload"; for my $value(unpack("C*",$buf)){$min=$value if $value<$min; $max=$value if $value>$max; $seen{$value}=1} $left-=$want} my $span=$max-$min; my $direct_bits=$span<=31?5:$span<=63?6:$span<=127?7:8; my $count=scalar keys %seen; my $dictionary_bits=$count<=32?5:$count<=64?6:$count<=128?7:8; push @rows,[$layer,$bytes,$min,$max,$span,$count,$direct_bits,$dictionary_bits]; $unique{$count}++; $bits{"direct:$direct_bits"}++; $bits{"dictionary:$dictionary_bits"}++; }} @rows=sort{$a->[0]<=>$b->[0]}@rows; print join("	",qw(layer bytes min max span unique direct_bits dictionary_bits)),"
"; print join("	",@$_),"
" for @rows; print "unique=",join(",",map{"$_:$unique{$_}"}sort{$a<=>$b}keys %unique),"
"; print "bits=",join(",",map{"$_:$bits{$_}"}sort keys %bits),"
";'
reproduction.safetensors_offset_rule: the first eight bytes are a little-endian U64 header length; each tensor data offset is relative to byte 8 + header_length
reproduction.payload_read_policy: seek directly to each selected tensor and scan its exact payload in 1-MiB chunks
reproduction.classification: track raw-code min, max, and a 256-entry presence set per layer; derive direct width from span and dictionary width from distinct-code count

claim_limits: This is a zero-code payload-ceiling rejection. There is no candidate binary, GPU timing, kernel result, end-to-end result, or achieved speedup.
The direct and dictionary payloads are ideal padding-free lower bounds; production would retain canonical scales for Prefill and fallbacks, so these values are not model-memory reductions.
The dictionary payload excludes even its small codebooks and all lookup cost, making 5.172413793% an optimistic byte ceiling rather than an implementation result.

The millisecond values linearly scale prior isolated scale6 projections by incremental byte saving and assume zero new overhead. They are screening estimates, not measured latency or guaranteed upper bounds.
The scan covers exactly the pinned 64 down-projection scale tensors on the locally materialized revision; it does not generalize to another checkpoint revision or projection family.
Production remains unchanged at 105.870500 ms/token / 9.445501816 token/s.
